name: Seer's Sundial
oracle_text: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, you may pay {2}. If you do, draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, you may pay {2}. If you do, draw a card.

needs.what: an optional mana cost payable by the ability's controller while a triggered ability is resolving -- e.g. `{"op": "may", "pay": {"mana": "{2}"}, "effects": [{"op": "draw", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}` -- where the mana is actually paid out of the pool (with mana abilities activatable to make it) and the wrapped effects happen only when the payment completes
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Every cost in reference is attached to the object being cast or activated, never to an effect mid-resolution: `Cost` (engine/carddef.py) carries mana, tap, untap, sacrifice, discard, discard_self, pay_life, remove_counters and exile_from_graveyard, and it is only ever read when a spell is cast or an ability is activated. The trigger here fires on its own and its effects run with no cost hook at all, so the {2} would simply have to be dropped -- turning a card that draws for {2} a land into one that draws free

needs.what: the yes/no prompt for that optional payment must be priced: offered only when the player can actually afford {2}, and its answer must be readable as the condition for the 'If you do' branch, so declining or being unable to pay skips the draw
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `may` (engine/effects/ops_control.py) is the only optional-effect op and it asks a bare yes/no with nothing at stake -- it takes `player`, `prompt`, `condition`, `effects`, `else` and `repeat`, but no cost, and it never consults affordability. Its `condition` and the `if` op both evaluate board conditions, and no condition in the vocabulary can read whether a mana payment was made, so 'If you do' has no source of truth to branch on. The nearest existing shape, `unless_pays` (Rhystic Study), is a different mechanic: it routes the payment to another player and inverts the outcome
